transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dave Mattingly.
This is Election Day across the U.S.
Voters will decide which party controls Congress come January.
NPR's Domenico Montanaro says Democrats are hoping to flip the slim Republican majorities in the House and Senate.
Democrats are the clear favorites to win the House.
The Senate is a toss-up.
Polling is showing things trending Democrats' way.
But a lot of these races are still within the margin of error, and we really can't predict what's going to happen.
The key Senate races include ones in Texas, Michigan, and Alaska.
Millions of people took part in early voting.
Open enrollment is underway across the U.S. for Affordable Care Act plans.
NPR's Maham Javed says the rising cost of health care is a big issue for many voters this year, especially in Florida.
Voters are considering the rising cost of health care as they decide their ballot this year.
This is especially true in states like Florida, where ACA enrollment is high because of the thriving gig economy and lack of Medicaid expansion.
Many Floridians lost coverage this year after the Trump administration let COVID-era federal subsidies expire.
Deanna Johnson lives in a competitive swing district in South Florida.
She can't afford health insurance.
I voted for the red last time, but this time now I'm thinking about voting blue to get our country back in order.
For many, health insurance is one more bill they can no longer afford, and they want their vote to fix that.
Maham Javed, NPR News, Henry County, Florida.
The National Transportation Safety Board says there's evidence suggesting a business jet that crashed in South Florida over the weekend started to break apart before it hit the ground and exploded in a fireball.
All nine people aboard the Learjet were killed when it crashed about seven miles southwest of West Palm Beach.
Those killed included a couple and their two young children.
North Korea is denying it was behind last week's theft of more than $6 billion from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange.
As NPR's Anthony Kuhn reports from Seoul, it's being called the largest such theft on record.
In a statement carried by state media, North Korean leader Kim Jong-un's sister Kim Yo-jong called the FBI's Saturday announcement that Pyongyang was behind the hack,
a political provocation, absurd rhetoric, and proof of the U.S.'s hostile policies towards Pyongyang.
She added that North Korea's consistent policy is to oppose malicious acts in cyberspace.
The FBI attributed the hack to Traitor Traitor, a subunit of cyber operatives under North Korean military intelligence.
The FBI and crypto researchers observed the hackers unauthorized transactions in public blockchain records and listed the addresses of accounts linked to North Korea, which received the transferred funds.
Anthony Kuhn in PR News, Seoul.
This is NPR News from Washington.
New York is reporting its first death from measles in 30 years.
State health officials say a child living north of Syracuse has died of the disease.
Health officials in Pennsylvania have reported five measles deaths this year and say they're investigating a potential sixth death.
Jury selection is underway in the federal trial of two members of Major League Baseball's Cleveland Guardians.
The two, both pitchers, are accused of accepting bribes to rig pitches for gamblers, as NPR's Becky Sullivan reports.
Cleveland's all-star pitcher Emmanuel Klasse was one of the best closers in baseball when prosecutors say he threw at least 18 rigged pitches.
All of them, the first pitch of the ninth inning, all of them in the dirt, are far off the plate.
Betters allegedly won at least $460,000 by placing scores of total wagers, making specific bets about those pitches.
Prosecutors say the scheme lasted for at least two years.
Another Guardians pitcher, Luis Ortiz, is accused of throwing rigged pitches at two games in 2025.
The trial is expected to last about a month.
Witnesses will include teammates and baseball executives.
Both players have pleaded not guilty to charges of fraud, sports, bribery, and money laundering.
If convicted, they face decades of prison time.
Becky Sullivan in PR News.
Meteorologists say a supercharged El Niño warming cycle in the Pacific Ocean is what's intensifying rainfall
than the southwestern U.S.
That's where flooding has been an issue in recent days and weeks.
Flash flooding caused evacuations in northern New Mexico, central Arizona, and areas of Colorado over the weekend.
I'm Dave Mattingly, NPR News, in Washington.
Get NPR+ at plus.npr.org.
That's plus.npr.org.

topics.text: Election Day voting underway nationwide, with Democrats favored to flip the House and the Senate a toss-up
Florida voters weigh rising ACA health insurance costs as open enrollment begins, with lapsed COVID-era subsidies
NTSB says a Learjet crashed near West Palm Beach, Florida, killing all nine aboard, may have broken apart midair
North Korea denies involvement in $6 billion Binance crypto theft, calling FBI attribution a political provocation
New York reports first measles death in 30 years, a child north of Syracuse; Pennsylvania has five measles deaths
Jury selection begins in federal trial of two Cleveland Guardians pitchers accused of rigging pitches for gamblers
El Niño warming cycle intensifies rainfall and flash flooding across the Southwest, prompting evacuations in New Mexico, Arizona, Colorado
